title: Odile and the Tide
premise: Ines Pemberton, a widowed single mother running Saltwick's only bookshop, has trained her heart into careful containment — until she hires Theo Marchetti, the town's disgraced former coastguard, to pose as her date for her family's reunion. The fake romance turns real just as Theo's private investigation into the wreck that killed Ines's husband collides with her family's secrets, revealing that the 'accident' was covered up by the very relatives whose approval Ines craves. As evidence surfaces and the town turns on them, Ines must choose between protecting her daughter's stability and pursuing justice outside the law, while Theo risks his last chance at reinstatement. They end not with legal vindication but with truth spoken aloud, a rebuilt bookshop, and a love that stops lending pieces and gives everything.
about_author: Rosalind Iversen is the pen name of a former coastal bookseller who spent a decade cataloguing tide charts and love stories in equal measure. She writes romances about people who mistake caution for safety, from a cottage within earshot of the North Sea.

chapters.title: The Muscle of the Heart
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Opening in Pemberton's Books during a storm, Ines rehearses her philosophy: hearts are trainable muscles, containable like any other. Her daughter Poppy asks why Mummy never dances anymore. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness disguised as discipline.

chapters.title: A Man Who Reads Marginalia
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Theo Marchetti returns a damaged secondhand novel, its margins annotated in his late father's hand; he and Ines argue over whether to repair or preserve it. She notices his coastguard tattoo half-sanded away. Beat: reluctant fascination.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Her mother summons her to the family reunion at Fairlight House, where her brother-in-law Charles will announce his parliamentary candidacy. Ines needs a respectable plus-one. Beat: dread sharpening into desperation.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Ines offers Theo money to play her boyfriend; he refuses payment but accepts anyway, needing access to Fairlight House, where his old coastguard logs were sealed after the wreck that killed her husband Daniel. Beat: guilt entwined with curiosity.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Over fish and chips they invent their history — how they met, first kiss, favorite songs — until the invented details feel dangerously true. Poppy catches them holding hands. Beat: warmth neither will name.

chapters.title: Fairlight House
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Arrival at the reunion: cold marble, colder mother, Charles's polished charm. Theo plays his role too well, charming even Ines's formidable grandmother. Beat: performance curdling into authenticity.

chapters.title: Dessert
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. By dessert the fake date feels real; under the table their hands find each other honestly. Then Charles makes a toast honoring Daniel's 'tragic accident,' and Theo watches Ines flinch. Beat: love arriving exactly as the lie collapses.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Alone in Fairlight's boathouse, Theo finds his confiscated logbook pages — readings proving the warning buoy was disabled the night Daniel died. He pockets them without telling Ines. Beat: duty versus desire, both losing.

chapters.title: First Real Kiss
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Walking the tideline after the reunion, Ines confronts Theo about what he's hiding; instead of answers he kisses her, and it is nothing like the rehearsed one. Beat: surrender she immediately regrets.

chapters.title: The Sealed File
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo contacts his old coastguard mentor, learning the investigation was closed from above — by someone connected to Fairlight House. His reinstatement hearing is scheduled in six weeks; silence could buy it back. Beat: the cost of truth made concrete.

chapters.title: Poppy's Question
chapters.summary: Poppy's POV (childlike third). Poppy likes Theo, who fixes her bicycle and reads her pirate stories, but asks Ines if new daddies replace old ones. Ines lies badly. Beat: innocence forcing honesty Ines isn't ready for.

chapters.title: Charles's Warning
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Charles visits the bookshop, offering to fund its expansion if Ines keeps her coastguard friend quiet. He mentions Theo's disciplinary record. Ines realizes her family knew something about the wreck. Beat: betrayal wearing a helpful face.

chapters.title: Confession at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo shows Ines the logbook pages: the buoy was sabotaged, Daniel's boat steered into dead water. Ines's grief reorganizes into fury — and suspicion of everyone she loves. Beat: shared purpose igniting alongside shared love.

chapters.title: The Grandmother's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines searches Fairlight's attic and finds her grandmother's ledgers recording payments to a marine engineer the month after the wreck. The grandmother, dying and lucid, tells her to burn them. Beat: inheritance revealed as complicity.

chapters.title: Middle of It
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Theo and Ines become lovers properly now, no pretense left, hiding copies of evidence in the bookshop's rare-book room. The town begins whispering. Beat: the calm center before the storm, deliberately tender.

chapters.title: Broken Window
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The bookshop window is smashed overnight; the evidence box is gone, though Theo kept duplicates. A note warns him off before his hearing. Ines blames herself. Beat: fear testing whether love can hold weight.

chapters.title: Hearing Day
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At his reinstatement hearing, Theo must choose: stay silent, regain his career, and abandon justice — or testify and end it. He testifies, submitting his testimony as a public statement. Beat: duty finally aligned with conscience.

chapters.title: Charles Unravels
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Charles's candidacy implodes as the engineer comes forward; confronted at Fairlight, Charles admits he disabled the buoy to cover an insurance fraud his father began. Ines records nothing — she simply walks out. Beat: justice outside the law, chosen over revenge.

chapters.title: The Storm
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. A real storm hits; Poppy is stranded at the harbor with the tide rising. Theo, stripped of official standing, leads an unofficial rescue using the old coastguard methods, with Ines at his side. Beat: the community witnessing who they truly are.

chapters.title: After the Water
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Poppy is safe; the town, having watched Theo risk everything, rallies to rebuild the shop. Ines's mother arrives not to apologize but to ask how to begin. Ines lets her try. Beat: forgiveness offered, not owed.

chapters.title: Everything, Not Pieces
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo, reinstated, chooses instead to co-run a maritime heritage trust with the bookshop as its home. He asks Ines for everything, not pieces. She says yes before he finishes asking. Beat: the contained heart, fully spent.

chapters.title: Odile and the Tide
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, epilogue one year later. At the shop's reopening, Poppy dances on the counter; the repaired marginalia novel sits in the window, its annotations finished by three hands now. Ines teaches customers that hearts are trainable — to be brave. Beat: memory honored, love permanent.
